text:
anita: Heads-up — since last Friday we've seen a spike in spot evictions in us-west-2 when the autoscaler mixes p4d + t4g pools. cost wins but eviction rate jumped from 0.9% -> 5.6% on production inference fleet. Anyone else seeing correlated network flaps or AZ-level pressure?

mike: yup noticed it. p95 latency bump too. My hunch is binpacking is squeezing too many different instance families into single hosts which increases chance of interruption correlated across the AZ.

lucas: Can you drop the eviction histogram? curious if it's concentrated on particular instance types or instance lifecycle times.

anita: pasted short stats from last 24h: 
```
evictions_by_type: { p4d: 38, a10g: 12, t4g: 84 }
eviction_rate_24h: 5.6%
p95_latency_tokens: 210ms -> 260ms
mean_runtime_sec: 42s
```

sam: hmm t4g seems noisy but also cheaper. Are we cross-az balancing? If our scheduler packs by bin (cpu+gpu) we might be losing diversification because spot price surge affects multiple instance types similarly in same AZ.

mike: exactly. Two knobs to try: 1) diversify by AZ and instance family (explicit anti-affinity for same spot-signal group), 2) add graceful fallback lanes so LBs can route short jobs to stable reserved nodes when eviction risk > X.

anita: thinking config change: restrict mixed-family packing on the same host and add a preemptible-score threshold that prevents bursting into lower-cost types during high market volatility. sketch: 
```
placement:
  allow_mixed_families_on_host: false
  diversification:
    by_az: true
    min_unique_families_per_pool: 2
preemptible_thresholds:
  eviction_risk_pct: 3.0
  fallback_reserve_pct: 8
```

ops-bot: @anita created incident INC-2026-241 and scheduled a rolling policy change at 03:00 UTC for testing.

lucas: +1 for a conservative flag to avoid aggressive packing. Also suggest we measure cross-instance eviction correlation: build a tiny job that starts on several instance families and logs preemption events with host metadata.

sam: quick experiment idea: run a 24h mixed fleet with two modes: "spreadpack" (spread families across hosts) vs "binpack" (pack by utilization). Compare average unit-cost, eviction rate, tail-latency. We should capture: tokens-per-dollar, p99 latency, grace-period failures.

mike: can prototype with this command on test cluster: 
```
./fleetctl create-experiment \
  --name spreadpack-vs-binpack \
  --duration 24h \
  --instance-types p4d,a10g,t4g \
  --modes spreadpack,binpack \
  --workload inference-small
```

anita: I'll run the prototype tonight. Sam, can you add dashboards for eviction-correlation matrix (rows: instance_type, cols: AZ) and a simple cost per token panel? Lucas please script the cross-instance preemption tracer.

lucas: on it. I'll use the node-metadata API and publish events to /metrics/preemption_trace. Quick sketch for tracer: 
```
GET /node/metadata -> {az, instance_type, spot_signal}
spawn job -> while alive: write(preempt_event, node_meta)
```

sam: one more note: if we split traffic by request length and route long prefixes to reserved/dedicated pools we can reduce tail impact during evictions. Might be low-effort and high-return.

mike: agree. Also add a safety cap: if regional spot volatility > 7% revert autoscaler to stable pool only.

anita: thanks all. Plan: 1) run experiment tonight, 2) dashboards + tracer by EOD, 3) conservative placement flag rollout to canary tomorrow. Will report results in this thread. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: @anita scheduled job spreadpack-vs-binpack (id: ex-3921) to start 03:15 UTC.

mike: thanks — if experiment shows spreadpack keeps eviction <2% while only increasing unit-cost <8%, we should adopt as default for spot pools.

anita: noted — will include tokens/dollar delta and p99 regressions in report.

lucas: small heads-up: check NIC-level throttling counters too (we saw that cause eviction-like behavior last quarter).

anita: good call. adding NIC counters to tracer.

sam: ping me when dashboards live, will review SLA impact.

anita: will do.
